message:
/speckit-specify I want a small command-line to-do app in Node.js (no npm dependencies).

Create `todo.js` at the project root, run as `node todo.js <command>`. Store todos in `todos.json` in the curr
result:
The to-do app is built and all 9 tests pass (`node --test test/todo.test.js`, Node v22).

**What I added**
- **`todo.js`**: the app, with no npm dependencies. It does `add`, `list`, `list --pending`, `done` and `remove`, with the exact output and exit codes you specified. `todos.json` is created in the current directory the first time something is saved. The file also stores the next ID to use, so IDs are never reused, even after every todo has been removed.
- **`test/todo.test.js`**: tests that run the real command in a fresh temporary folder each time. They check the exact output, exit codes, that errors go to stderr, and that a failed command leaves `todos.json` unchanged.
- **Spec**: `specs/001-todo-cli/spec.md`, with its quality checklist at `specs/001-todo-cli/checklists/requirements.md`. Every checklist item passed and no clarification questions were needed. `.specify/feature.json` points to this folder, so `/speckit-plan` would pick it up next if you want the full spec-kit workflow. No extension hooks are set up in this project.

**Choices I made where your request didn't say**
- `add Buy milk` without quotes joins the words into `Buy milk`. Empty or blank text counts as missing text.
- A missing, non-numeric, zero, negative or decimal ID is treated as an unknown ID: error, exit code 1.
- Running `done` on a todo that's already done succeeds and prints `Done <id>` again.
- An unknown option such as `list --foo`, or running with no command at all, is an error with exit code 1.
- If `todos.json` exists but isn't valid, the app shows an error and exits with 1 rather than overwriting it.

Nothing is committed yet.

The plan is written, and the design it describes matches the `todo.js` that already exists. No code changed.

I checked the docs against the real app: running the quickstart's manual commands in a scratch folder gave exactly the documented output and exit codes.

The setup script reports the branch as `001-todo-cli`, taken from the feature folder name. That branch doesn't exist; you're still on `main`, and nothing is committed yet.

**Files in `specs/001-todo-cli/`:**
- **`plan.md`**: setup details, structure (a single `todo.js` plus `test/todo.test.js`) and the constitution check.
- **`research.md`**: eight design decisions with reasons. The main ones:
  - IDs come from a saved `nextId` counter rather than `max(id) + 1`, which would hand out a removed ID again.
  - `todos.json` is written to a temporary file first and then renamed into place, so a crash can't leave it half-written.
  - A corrupt `todos.json` is reported and never overwritten.
  - An ID must be a positive whole number.
- **`data-model.md`**: the Todo and the file layout, what must always hold true, and how a todo moves from pending to done to removed.
- **`contracts/cli.md`**: each command's exact output and its error cases.
- **`quickstart.md`**: how to run the tests, plus a step-by-step manual check.

The constitution (`.specify/memory/constitution.md`) is still the blank template, so there were no project rules to check against. I used basic checks instead (simplest structure, output and errors to the right streams, tests in place), and all of them passed before and after the design. No extension hooks are set up.

Next step is `/speckit-tasks`. Since the code and tests are already done, the resulting task list would just record finished work.

I wrote the task list at `specs/001-todo-cli/tasks.md`: 20 tasks, of which 19 are already done and checked off. The one open task, T020, is a speed check that hasn't been run yet.

The app and its tests were built before this list existed, so ticking the boxes records work already done and tested (9 of 9 tests pass, and the quickstart output matched). I included test tasks because you asked me to "build it, test it".

| Phase | Tasks | Count | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Setup | T001–T002 | 2 | done |
| 2. Foundational (file storage, error handling, command handling) | T003–T006 | 4 | done |
| 3. US1 add and list (P1, MVP) | T007–T009 | 3 | done |
| 4. US2 done and `--pending` (P2) | T010–T013 | 4 | done |
| 5. US4 error feedback (P2) | T014–T015 | 2 | done |
| 6. US3 remove without reusing IDs (P3) | T016–T017 | 2 | done |
| 7. Final checks | T018–T020 | 3 | 2 done, **T020 open** |

**How each story is checked on its own:**
- **US1:** in an empty folder, add two todos, and `list` shows `1 [ ] …` and `2 [ ] …`. Listing with no todos prints `No todos`.
- **US2:** after `done 1`, `list --pending` shows only todo 2.
- **US4:** every error case exits with code 1, writes only to stderr, and leaves `todos.json` unchanged.
- **US3:** add three todos, remove 3, then add one more, and it gets `Added 4: …`.

**Still open, T020:** the spec says every command should finish in under a second with 1,000 todos. No test checks that yet; T020 adds one.

**Running in parallel:** very little, because the app is one file. The test file and `todo.js` can be worked on side by side (the test setup alongside the core of `todo.js`, and each story's tests alongside its code). All the code changes go into `todo.js`, so they have to happen one after another.

**Order:** US2's `--pending` builds on US1's `list`. US3's `remove` reuses the ID-lookup code written for US2's `done`. The tasks file notes both.

**Suggested MVP:** User Story 1 only (T001–T009).

**Format:** all 20 tasks follow the required line format: checkbox, task ID, `[P]` and story labels where they apply, and a file path. No extension hooks are set up.

Next, `/speckit-implement` would only need to do T020. Or run `/speckit-analyze` first to check the spec, plan and tasks agree with each other.

All 20 tasks are done: the to-do app meets the spec, and all 10 tests pass (`node --test test/todo.test.js`).

**What this run did:**
- **T020, the speed check:** I added a test that loads 1,000 todos, then runs `list`, `add`, `done` and `remove`, failing if any of them takes 1 second or more. All five commands it runs took about 130 ms in total, so roughly 25 ms each. That confirms the speed goal in the spec (SC-002).
- **`.gitignore`:** the repo didn't have one, so I created it with the usual Node and editor entries. It also ignores `todos.json`, since that file holds a user's own todos rather than project code.
- **Docs:** `tasks.md` and `quickstart.md` now say 10 passing tests instead of 9. All tasks are marked done, with 0 left open.

**Checks:** the spec-quality checklist passed, with all 16 items ticked. The app matches the spec's command outputs, exit codes and error behaviour, and follows the plan: a single `todo.js` using only Node's built-in modules, plus black-box tests. No extension hooks are set up.

The work is still uncommitted on `main` (`todo.js`, `test/`, `specs/`, `.gitignore`); I can commit it if you'd like.
